headline: Profit grows faster than sales as comps stay soft
summary_short: Domino's revenue rose 3.4% y/y to $1,185.6M and diluted EPS rose 12.7% to $4.60, as operating income grew 8.3% despite only 0.3% U.S. same store sales growth.
summary_long: Revenue growth came from higher supply chain revenue (volumes and a 2.2% higher food basket price) and franchise royalties on net store growth, partly offset by lower company-owned store revenue after U.S. refranchising. Supply chain gross margin rose 0.9 points on procurement productivity. Operating income rose 8.3% to $241.8M. EPS growth also reflected a lower diluted share count from buybacks. Global retail sales rose 3.2% ex-FX, with 175 net new stores (26 U.S., 149 international). Year-to-date free cash flow was $459.8M, down from $495.6M. A $1.99 quarterly dividend was declared. No numeric guidance was given.
confidence_notes: The release shows diluted EPS of $4.60; the shard's $4.61 is SEC basic EPS, so the diluted figure is used here. First-quarter 2026 operating income included a gain on the sale of the corporate aircraft, which affects year-to-date free cash flow comparisons only. Joe Jordan's first quarter as CEO per the release.

drivers.explanation: Higher supply chain revenues from order volumes and a 2.2% higher food basket price, plus higher franchise royalties from net store growth; partly offset by lower company-owned store revenues after refranchising.
Higher U.S. and international franchise royalties and fees plus gross margin dollar growth in supply chain; supply chain margin rose 0.9 points on procurement productivity.
Higher net income and a lower weighted average diluted share count from share repurchases over the trailing four quarters.
175 net openings in the quarter, 26 in the U.S. and 149 internationally.
New CEO Joe Jordan said Domino's will build on its brand, franchise system and scale to earn more occasions and keep gaining market share.
